transport: 3-terminal hardwiring block marked "EXT.SW" (terminals S / – / +) · 2-wire dry contact: short S to – = ON, open = OFF · or 2-wire switched DC 10–33 VDC on + / – into an internal opto-isolator · or 1-wire switched battery voltage · front-panel 3-position rocker must FIRST be pushed to the bottom "EXT. Switch" position · wiring AWG #22
sharedMapEvidence: One Samlex owner's manual, 11001-PST-1500-2000-12-24_1221, is titled for and covers PST-1500-12, PST-1500-24, PST-2000-12 and PST-2000-24 together, with a single layout figure (Fig 6.1) and a single external-control section (§8.9) applying to all four. The terminal block is item 4A in that one shared figure.
gotchas: Open loop. The EXT.SW block is an input only — nothing on it reports back. Cabin Hub can command set-switch and cannot observe whether the inverter actually came up. Any state must come from an external AC sensor (a PZEM on the output, say), not from the inverter.
The rocker switch is a hard prerequisite. If somebody leaves the front rocker in the centre or top position, the relay does nothing and there is no way to detect that over the wire.

Not the same wiring as the PST-3000. That model uses a 4-terminal block and accepts 10–60 VDC; this one is 3 terminals and 10–33 VDC. Deliberately catalogued as separate dialects — a 48 V control signal on this block is out of spec.
The switched-DC input is opto-isolated, so the external control source's ground is isolated from the battery negative. A 1 A fuse close to the DC source is required by the manual.

Documentation error in the vendor PDF: Fig 8.2(c) in this manual captions the 1-wire example as "+12V from 12V battery feeding PST-600-12 / +24V from 24V battery feeding PST-600-24" — copy-paste from the PST-600 manual. The figure is in the PST-1500/2000 book.
